atoms.b: Rosa’s brave protest had a ((tiny ++massive)) impact on the fight against racism in America.
She inspired around ((++40,000 2)) people to stop using the bus service in Montgomery for over a year!

instruction.text: What do you think was the impact of nobody taking the bus?

hint.text: Remember that 40,000 people stopped taking the bus!

feedback.end: The Montgomery bus boycott forced the bus company to change their segregation rules!

b.sound: The bus company made more money.

instruction.text: You’re talking to a historian about what came next. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: What happened after the Montgomery ((car ++bus)) boycott?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'>What happened after the Montgomery bus boycott?</prosody>

atoms.b: Rosa’s protest sparked the civil rights movement, which aimed to ((start ++get_rid)) of segregation and discrimination across America.
After a long struggle, a ((shop ++law)) called the Civil Rights Act was finally passed in 1964.
This made it illegal to treat people ((++differently the_same)) because of their race or religion.

feedback.finish: Rosa’s protest was inspirational, and many people see her as the “mother of the civil rights movement”.

atoms.a: Do you think Rosa should have been proud of her achievements?

finish.text: Rosa’s story shows us that even small, courageous acts of protest can inspire big changes.
